latest.question: Deputy Sean Fleming asked the Minister for Social Protection for an overview of the Budget 2027 supports for pensioners.
latest.reply:
Over €13 billion was allocated to State Pensions in Budget 2027, which is an increase of almost €1 billion compared with Budget 2026.
There will be a €10 increase in the maximum weekly rate of all State Pensions from January 2027. This means the State Pension (Contributory) will exceed €300 per week for the first time at a maximum rate of €309.30. The State Pension (Non-Contributory) will increase to a maximum weekly rate of €298. There will be proportionate increases for qualified adults and people getting a reduced rate of pension.
The Living Alone Increase is increasing to €25 per week from January, the first increase to the payment in five years. This payment has increased by nearly 178% since 2019, when it was just €9 per week.
Budget 2027 also provides for a €5 increase in Fuel Allowance, from €38 to €43 per week. This represents an additional €140 over the fuel season and will bring the total annual value of the payment to over €1,200. Budget 2027 also improves access to Fuel Allowance for older people by increasing the means threshold for single pensioners. The income limit for a single person aged 66 or over will increase from 50% to 60% of the corresponding limit for a couple.
In addition, from July 2027 the upper income threshold for the Increase for a Qualified Adult in relation to the State Pension (Contributory) and other social insurance schemes will increase from €310 to €340 per week.

latest.question: Deputy John Clendennen asked the Minister for Social Protection the measures being taken by his department to improve awareness and uptake of the Household Benefits Package among eligible people, particularly those aged 70 and over; and whether an automatic enrolment of eligible recipients would be considered.
latest.reply:
The Household Benefits package is available to those aged 70 or over regardless of means and household composition, however there is no automatic entitlement to the payment and similar to many other Social Welfare benefits a person aged over 70 must submit an application form to determine entitlement.
To qualify for the Household Benefits Package applicants aged over 70 must be legally resident in the State and no other person in their household can be in receipt of the allowance. An applicant must also be the registered consumer of electricity/gas if she or he is applying for an Electricity Allowance or Natural Gas Allowance and must also register for the Public Services Card when requested to do so by the department.
Taking the above into consideration, the introduction of automatic enrolment of eligible recipients would not be practical and therefore cannot be considered at this time.
With regards to improving awareness and uptake of the Household Benefits Package, information regarding the Household Benefits Package is widely available in Department of Social Protection and Citizen’s Information offices, and online through the Gov.ie and Citizen Information websites.
To further increase awareness of the scheme my Department launched a public information campaign to promote the Household Benefit Package. This was launched on 12th October and advertisements feature across regional radio and social media channels until 15th November.

latest.question: Deputy Peter Roche asked the Minister for Social Protection whether consideration is being given to extending eligibility for domiciliary care allowance from 16 to age 18 years-of-age; the rationale for the current age limit; and the review undertaken or planned in this regard.
latest.reply:
I propose to take Questions Nos. 77 and 94 together.
Domiciliary Care Allowance is a payment to a parent or guardian in respect of a child under 16 who has a severe disability and requires continuous care and attention, substantially more than is typically required by a child of the same age.
From January 2026, the monthly rate of Domiciliary Care Allowance increased from €360 to €380. Over 66,600 families receive Domiciliary Care Allowance in respect of approximately 76,400 children, with estimated expenditure of almost €359 million in 2026.
Domiciliary Care Allowance stops being paid when a child turns 16 years of age. A young person whose disability significantly impacts their daily living activities may then apply for Disability Allowance in their own right, which is currently payable at a maximum personal rate of €254 per week. To help avoid a gap in support, an application for Disability Allowance can be made up to three months before the young person’s 16th birthday.
Where the young person's carer is also receiving Carer's Allowance or Carer's Benefit, those payments may continue for as long as the relevant qualifying conditions continue to be met. The carer may also continue to qualify for the annual Carer's Support Grant of €2,000 where the qualifying conditions are met.
There are no plans to extend Domiciliary Care Allowance from age 16 to 18 years at this time.

latest.question: Deputy Ruairí Ó Murchú asked the Minister for Social Protection the steps he will take to ensure that seasonal workers, including those who work in schools, who lose working family payment during holiday time, do not have to wait six or eight weeks when employment resumes to get their WFP back in payment.
latest.reply:
Working Family Payment (WFP), formerly Family Income Supplement, is a weekly in-work support which provides an income top-up for employees on low earnings with children. To qualify for Working Family Payment the customer must be working a minimum of 38 hours per fortnight in ongoing insurable employment and have at least 1 qualified child who normally resides with them.
The Department is committed to providing a quality service to all its customers. This includes ensuring that applications are processed as quickly as possible, currently within 4 weeks.
Working Family Payment (WFP) new claim applications have increased by 27% in 2026, with 58,764 customers currently in receipt of the payment compared to 51,323 at the beginning of the year. The number of WFP claims for Educational Sector Workers requiring reinstatement during the same period has also increased significantly. Despite this increased workload, processing times have remained in line with the 2025 levels, and all outstanding ESW cases were cleared by mid to late October 2026.
I trust this clarifies the matter for the Deputy.

latest.question: Deputy Louise O'Reilly asked the Minister for Social Protection for an update on the rate of rejected domiciliary care allowance applications subsequently overturned on appeal; and the average length of time taken to process an appeal.
latest.reply:
There is no direct correlation between the number and percentage of Domiciliary Care Allowance decisions and the number of appeals registered during a particular time period. Timing differences will always apply. This is particularly the case since the Appeal Regulations which came into effect from April 2025 increased the number of days a person has to make an appeal from 21 days to 60 days. Accordingly appeals received in January 2026 may refer to decisions made in November 2025.
However, as an indication of the appeal rate, 4,864 Domiciliary Care Allowance applications were rejected up to end of Quarter 3 2026. The number of Domiciliary Care Allowance appellants who received a favourable decision on their appeal in the same period of time was 1,918. This indicates that 39% of those who appealed received a favourable decision.
Where an appeal is successful it does not always indicate that the original decision was incorrect. In many cases, an appellant submits additional information or evidence during the review or appeals process that was not available to the Deciding Officer when the original decision was determined. This can result in a different decision being made on review or appeal.
The average timeframe to process all appeals up to end of Quarter 3 2026 was 10.7 weeks. The average timeframe to process Domiciliary Care Allowance appeals for the same period was 9 weeks.
The Chief Appeals Officer continues to monitor processing times and every effort is made to reduce

latest.question: Deputy Brendan Smith asked the Minister for Social Protection to report on the findings of the nutritional review and survey on hot school meals.
latest.reply:
The key finding in the Nutrition Review report was there is a wide variety of healthy meals on offer. 82% of meal options reviewed did not contain foods considered to be high in fat, salt or sugar such as chicken goujons, sausages or fried potato products. However, when data on meals ordered was analysed, it is evident that high, fat ,salt and sugar foods are chosen over healthier options when available on the menu.
There was a total of 18 recommendations. The Government has already accepted these recommendations, and work has commenced to implement them over the next 12 months.
These include increasing the provision of fruit, vegetables and wholegrain foods, improving some recipes that are higher in fat and salt than desirable, strengthening nutritional provision in vegetarian and vegan meals, ensuring age-appropriate portion sizes and enhancing menu options for children with special dietary requirements.
Nutrition Standards for Hot School Meals have been in place since the inception of the scheme and were strengthened in 2025 through the removal of foods high in fat, salt and sugar from menus. Following the nutritional review, the standards have been revised and consolidated to remove ambiguity and further support compliance with national healthy eating guidelines.
My Department are now progressing a comprehensive implementation plan arising from the review. This includes the development of a standardised three week menu cycle, adapted menus for special schools and children

latest.question: Deputy Thomas Gould asked the Minister for Social Protection whether he intends to bring forward a cost of disability payment for disabled people not currently in receipt of a social welfare payment.
latest.reply:
I propose to take Questions Nos. 87 and 90 together.
The Government recognises the additional costs that disabled people can face in their daily lives and is committed to improving outcomes for disabled people by introducing permanent measures.
As a result of Budget 2027, over €30 billion will be spent on social welfare in 2027, including almost €1.15 billion in new measures.
In particular, in Budget 2027, the Government provided for the first ever Cost of Disability payment. This will be paid as a lump sum payment of €500 in the week beginning 15 February 2027 to people receiving a long-term working age disability payment, specifically Blind Pension, Disability Allowance, Invalidity Pension, Partial Capacity Benefit. The payment will be made to approximately 240,000 people at an estimated cost of €119 million in 2027.
The over 1,100 submissions received in the public consultation process earlier this year, the outputs of the Strategic Focus Network Summit I hosted in the Aviva Stadium in May, and the discussions I've had with disabled people and their advocates at several engagements in recent months have all informed the approach that we, across Government, have taken in Budget 2027.

latest.question: Deputy Thomas Gould asked the Minister for Social Protection the percentage of Domiciliary Care Allowance applications with addresses in Cork refused; and the percentage of these then accepted on appeal.
latest.reply:
Domiciliary Care Allowance is a monthly, non-means tested, payment to a parent or guardian for a child aged up to 16 who has a severe disability. The child must require care and attention substantially over and above that required by other children their age.
At the end of September 2026, there were 66,400 customers who were in receipt of Domiciliary Care Allowance in respect of 76,100 children. The number of children on Domiciliary Care Allowance has more than doubled since 2016.
Over the year to the end of September 2026, there were just over 13,200 decisions recorded for Domiciliary Care Allowance nationwide, of which 4,800, or 37%, were refusals. Over the same time, there were over 2,600 appeal decisions for Domiciliary Care Allowance. Of these, some 1,900, 14% of Domiciliary Care Allowance claims were decided in favour of the appellant. This includes where the applicant received a revised decision from my Department or where the claim was allowed or partially allowed by an Appeals Officer.
A claim that was initially refused, but later awarded on appeal, does not necessarily mean that the initial decision was incorrect. Every claim decision is made based on the evidence available to the Deciding Officer/Appeals Officer, with reference to the scheme eligibility criteria. latest.question: Deputy Seán Ó Fearghaíl asked the Minister for Social Protection for an overview of the Budget 2027 supports for carers.
latest.reply:
The main income supports to carers provided by my department are the Carer’s Allowance, Carer’s Benefit, Domiciliary Care Allowance and the Carer’s Support Grant. Next year the combined spending on these payments is estimated at almost €2.5 billion.
As part of Budget 2027, I announced a number of measures to support carers, these include:
- From January 2027 there will be a €10 increase in the maximum rate of Carer's Allowance and Carer's Benefit.
- From next July, there will be a further increase in the Carer's Allowance income disregard to €1,150 for a single person and €2,300 for a couple. This will mean that a working-age couple household can earn €126,000 annually and retain a full Carer’s Allowance payment. Even with an income of €156,000 a couple could still receive a partial Carer’s Allowance payment. Over the last two Budgets the income disregards have increased for single carers by a total of €525 and by €1,050 for carers who are part of a couple. These changes represent increases of 84%.
- The earnings limit for Carer’s Benefit will also increase next year to €1,150, after tax.
- Some 27,000 Carer’s Allowance recipients will benefit from the increase to the Fuel Allowance payment of €5 per week.

latest.question: Deputy Erin McGreehan asked the Minister for Social Protection his plans to review the means test for the qualified adult payment for pensions.
latest.reply:
My Department provides State Pension payments through the State Pension (Contributory), which is based on a person's social insurance record, and the State Pension (Non-Contributory), which is means-tested social assistance payment.
A State Pension (Contributory) recipient can claim an increase on their pension in respect of a qualified adult subject to a means test and where the eligibility conditions are satisfied. Only the means of the spouse or partner of the claimant are assessed. Where savings, property or other assets are held jointly, the spouse or partner's means is taken to be half of the total amount.
Article 7 of SI 142 of 2007, the Social Welfare (Consolidated Claims, Payments and Control) Regulations, as amended, sets out the income limit for the payment of an Increase for a Qualified Adult across a range of schemes, not solely in respect of the State Pension (Contributory) scheme.
An Increase for Qualified Adult is payable at the maximum rate of payment where the means of the qualified adult are not more than €100 per week.
Currently, reduced rates are payable where means are over €100 and not more than €310 per week. However, as I announced in Budget 2027, from July next year the upper threshold for qualified adults will increase to €340 for a number of schemes, thus enabling more pensioners to qualify for an increased payment in respect of their spouse or partner.
A review of means testing is currently at an advanced stage within my department and I expect it

latest.question: Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Social Protection if he will review the rules governing receipt of carer's allowance and carer's benefit with a view to increasing the maximum number of hours carers may engage in employment, self-employment, education or training outside the home, which is currently limited to 18.5 hours per week.
latest.reply:
My Department provides a comprehensive package of income supports for carers, including Carer’s Allowance, Carer’s Benefit, Domiciliary Care Allowance and the Carer’s Support Grant. Combined expenditure on these schemes in 2026 is expected to exceed €2.2 billion.
The primary objective of carers payments is to provide an income support to carers whose earning capacity is substantially reduced because of their full-time caring responsibilities.
A primary qualifying condition for Carer's Allowance and Carer's Benefit is that the applicant must be providing full-time care and attention. A person is regarded as providing full time care where they provide at least 35 hours of care per week, over any five days in a seven day period.
While carer income support payments are based on the provision of full-time care and attention, they also provide flexibility in terms of supporting carers to engage in work, training or education for up to 18.5 hours per week. During this time, adequate provision must be made for the care of the relevant person.
There are no plans to amend this condition at this time. In setting the relevant threshold, it is essential to balance the needs of the carer and the needs of the person receiving care. The 18.5-hour rule represents a reasonable balance between meeting the requirement for providing full-time care for the care recipient and the needs of the carer to engage in employment, education or training, supporting a carer’s continued connection to the work

examples.reply:
As previously advised to the Deputy, the school referred to was approved to enter my Department's pipeline of projects under the Additional School Accommodation (ASA) scheme.
The project received approval from my Department to commence construction in January 2026. More recently, Department officials were notified by the school authorities that construction has now commenced. Expected completion to coincide with the start of the new school year.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Donnelly asked the Minister for Defence if she is aware of Irish Defence Forces members participating in military competitions with the Israeli Defence Forces; and if confirmed, her views on such on participation.
examples.reply:
The Defence Forces participate in international military competitions in order to promote in the Defence Forces the adoption of international best practice, exchange of tactics, techniques and procedures (TTP) and encourage the development of military skills. It also contributes to the development of particular military skillsets and doctrines.
The decision on who to invite to these competitions lies with the hosting nation. I am informed by the military authorities that the Defence Forces have not participated in any military competitions organised by the Israeli Defence Forces. I am also informed that, to date, no Defence Forces team has reported Israeli Defence Forces participation in competitions attended by Defence Forces personnel.

examples.question: Deputy Erin McGreehan asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine for an update on the timeline and commencement dates for the basic income support for sustainability scheme.
examples.reply:
My Department is fully committed to making payments to farmers under the various schemes at the earliest date possible and to the maximum number of farmers possible. This commitment to farmers is evidenced in the very high payment rates achieved across all schemes over the last number of years in both EU and Exchequer funded schemes.
The timelines for all schemes, including the planned payment dates, have been set after extensive consultation with farmers and taking account of application systems, monitoring systems, validation and processing systems and payment systems.
In 2025, my Department commenced payments under the Basic Income Support for Sustainability (BISS) scheme from October 16th ensuring money flowed as soon as practically possible to farmers.
This payment date is in line with the traditional payment date of the BISS Scheme to farmers and is as outlined in the Farmers' Charter.

examples.question: Deputy Tom Brabazon asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage for an update on the financial contribution scheme; and the rationale to no longer fund this scheme.
examples.reply:
The Government’s new housing plan, Delivering Homes, Building Communities 2025-2030, includes measures to increase delivery of housing for older people through increased delivery of social housing, increased delivery of more suitable homes in private housing and increased choice to support voluntary rightsizing, including a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes.
I understand that existing financial contribution schemes in place in some local authorities are non-statutory and therefore a matter for the individual local authorities. Consideration will be given to a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes and my Department is advancing these measures now incorporated in the new housing plan.

examples.question: Deputy Réada Cronin asked the Minister for Climate, Energy and the Environment what specific regulatory changes are being sought by Re-Turn for the proposed rPET reprocessing facility; the Department's position on the establishment of such a processing facility.
examples.reply:
Re-turn is a producer-led and owned, not-for-profit company established by beverage producers to meet their obligations under the Separate Collection (Deposit Return Scheme) Regulations.
Re-turn has stated its ambition to develop an rPET reprocessing facility in Ireland. In this regard, Re-turn has briefed me and Departmental officials on its plans.
The matter remains under consideration, with the Department considering the various public policy considerations that arise.

examples.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Transport further to Parliamentary Question No.199 of 16 April 2026, regarding Ireland's current position (details supplied); whether he has articulated this position either internally with Irish officials or with European counterparts; if so, if he will provide details of what was articulated and through which medium.
examples.reply:
I am aware of the concerns raised by car rental fleet operators regarding the Clean Corporate Vehicles proposal. We engage regularly with representatives from this sector and have met with them several times over the past year, including discussions specifically on this proposal.
It should be noted that the measure remains at proposal stage, with negotiations currently underway at EU level. The Regulation will not be finalised until such time as an agreement is reached between the Council and the European Parliament. This process is expected to run through 2026, which intersects with Ireland’s Presidency of the Council of the EU.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Murphy asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine the numerical, scientific and editorial verification carried out before the Wildlife Unit End of Year Report for 2025 that was approved for publication; whether further errors have since been identified; and whether his Department will publish an amended report clearly identifying all corrections.
examples.reply:
The Wildlife Report compiled by my Department has stated that there was 7,625 badger captures in the vaccine area in 2025. This is the correct figure. The figure of 8,123 is the number of badger captures that were recorded in vaccine areas for 2024. Table 4 in the report states the correct figures of badger captures for 2024 and 2025.
For the purposes of clarity the figure for 2024 will be removed from the body of the text.

examples.question: Deputy Carol Nolan asked the Minister for Social Protection the number of people who have had their receipt of jobseeker's allowance or jobseeker's benefit permanently withdrawn or revoked for breach of the conditions associated with their claim, and who have not subsequently had their claim reinstated, from January 2020 to date.
examples.reply:
To be eligible for a Jobseeker's payment a person must satisfy all the eligibility criteria for the relevant scheme.
Where a claim has been stopped, it will only be re-instated following an application by the customer and where all conditions of the scheme are satisfied.
It is not possible to provide data on the number of claims stopped and not subsequently re-instated due to the large churn on jobseekers schemes and the many legitimate reasons that claims are stopped.
I trust that this clarifies matters for the Deputy.

examples.question: Deputy Ruth Coppinger asked the Minister for Social Protection the annual figures since 2015 for appeals lodged with the social welfare appeals office querying a refusal based on the habitual residence condition, by Irish citizens and non-Irish nationals, in tabular form.
examples.reply:
I am advised by the Chief Appeals Officer that the Social Welfare Appeals Office does not collate data on appeals specifically relating to the Habitual Residence Condition, therefore the statistical information is not available.
I trust this clarifies the matter for the Deputy.

examples.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage the number of appeals involving the rating of agricultural or horticultural buildings have been brought before the Valuation Tribunal since 2020; the number that were successful; and the average length of time taken to determine these appeals.
examples.reply:
As the Valuation Tribunal is independent in the performance of its functions, my Department does not hold the information requested in relation to the number of appeals involving the rating of agricultural or horticultural buildings have been brought before the Valuation Tribunal since 2020; the number that were successful; or the average length of time taken to determine these appeals.
It is noted that certain information on Valuation Tribunal appeals activity is included in the Tribunal's Annual Reports, available on the organisation's website at: www.valuationtribunal.ie/about-us/publications/.
Judgements of the Valuation Tribunal are also published and can be accessed on the Tribunal's website (at: www.valuationtribunal.ie/judgments/) under 'Name', 'Year', 'Property category' and 'Rating Authority'. It is noted that the Tribunal does not, however, include a specific category of appeal termed 'agriculture / horticultural'.
The Deputy may wish to contact the Tribunal directly in relation to the information sought by emailing info@valuationtribunal.ie.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Lawless asked the Minister for Transport for a record of all reported accidents, collisions, or safety incidents that have occurred at or in the vicinity of the unmarked traffic islands in Ballindine, County Mayo, on the N17, over the past 20 years; if road safety audits or assessments have been carried out at this location; and if there are plans to install appropriate road markings or safety measures at this site.
examples.reply:
As Minister for Transport, I have responsibility for overall policy and exchequer funding in relation to the National Roads Programme. Under the Roads Acts 1993-2015 and in line with the National Development Plan (NDP), the operation and management of individual national roads is a matter for Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII), in conjunction with the local authorities concerned. This is also subject to the Infrastructure Guidelines and the necessary statutory approvals. In this context, TII is best placed to advise you in relation to safety on the N17 at Ballindine, Co. Mayo.
The Government is committed to reducing road deaths and creating safer roads for everyone in Ireland.
Noting the above position, I have referred your question to TII for a direct reply. Please advise my private office if you do not receive a reply within 10 working days.
